messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: On the coming deprecation of ~
parts:
I see (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Stan-3-Density-Notation-and-Increments) that there has been discussion of replacing expressions like "y ~ normal(0,1)" with "target += normal(y|0,1)". 

With as much humility as I can express while simultaneously questioning the devs' design decisions, I wanted to express that I'm really going to miss the current "~" format. I feel like it helped me, and others I've taught, understand the creation of stan code as an exercise of model expression. I like that with the "~" format you can simply replace characters with words and retrieve grammatical english ( "y~ normal(0,1)" means we're asserting that y is distributed as unit normal...").  

I see that the argument was made that the use of "target +=" is more faithful to what Stan is doing behind the scenes computationally, and while I can't say I actually understand said background mechanics to see how the "~" format can lead to problematic misunderstanding, I have to wonder if the increased transparency to Stan's underlying mechanics is worth the more conceptually and visually cumbersome format. 

It certainly looks like we'll all be making keyboard shortcuts for typing "target += " :O/

Presumably I'm wrong or an outlier?

Mike

--
Mike Lawrence
Graduate Student
Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
Dalhousie University

~ Certainty is (possibly) folly ~

messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: Re: On the coming deprecation of ~
parts:
On Thursday, June 9, 2016 at 3:27:28 PM UTC-4, Mike Lawrence wrote:
I see (https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/Stan-3-Density-Notation-and-Increments) that there has been discussion of replacing expressions like "y ~ normal(0,1)" with "target += normal(y|0,1)".

I feel like it helped me, and others I've taught, understand the creation of stan code as an exercise of model expression. I like that with the "~" format you can simply replace characters with words and retrieve grammatical english ( "y~ normal(0,1)" means we're asserting that y is distributed as unit normal...").

The '~' seems to get interpreted in two ways that I can tell: 1) "is distributed as"; and 2) "is drawn from ...".  Both of them are wrong since we frequently state priors as, for example, "theta ~ normal(0,1)" when the posterior we sample from is very much not normal... so neither "is distributed as" or "is drawn from" apply.  Both misinterpretations result in a fair bit of mailing list traffic so this is an attempt at making things better.

I see that the argument was made that the use of "target +=" is more faithful to what Stan is doing behind the scenes computationally, and while I can't say I actually understand said background mechanics to see how the "~" format can lead to problematic misunderstanding, I have to wonder if the increased transparency to Stan's underlying mechanics is worth the more conceptually and visually cumbersome format. 

It certainly looks like we'll all be making keyboard shortcuts for typing "target += " :O/
Just replace the "_" shortcut for "<-"... :P
Presumably I'm wrong or an outlier?

I'm pretty sure you have Andrew and Bob (or at least part of Bob) on your side so you could be doing worse.

Krzysztof

Mike

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: On the coming deprecation of ~
parts: On Thursday, June 9, 2016 at 3:27:28 PM UTC-4, Mike Lawrence wrote:
Presumably I'm wrong or an outlier?

Neither. But far too many people are reading theta ~ normal(0,1) as "theta is drawn from a standard normal distribution". Even interpreting theta ~ normal(0,1) as "theta is distributed standard normal" is only correct if you add "a priori" to it. It wasn't an unambiguous decision, and I don't think we have decided how long ~ will continue to be valid syntax. But those of us who supported the change wanted to avoid perpetuating the misunderstandings about how the Stan language relates to the Stan algorithms.

Ben

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] On the coming deprecation of ~
parts:
Hi, yes, we've discussed this a lot at the Stan meetings.  There seems to be a real tradeoff here:  getting rid of ~ will make a lot of people miserable, on the other hand it could reduce some confusion.
I also have high hopes for a parser we've been talking about that will search Stan models for conceptual errors (things such as uniform priors and other bad modeling choices that are common).
A

messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] On the coming deprecation of ~
parts:
If I understand correctly, the key problem with ~ is that by hiding the
fact that it increments the log density, it confuses people who don't
understand the basics of Bayesian inference.

The implicit hypothesis behind the removal of ~ as a solution seems to
be that by forcing things to be explicit, people who are unfamiliar with
Bayesian inference will be forced to understand what is going on.

While I have my priors about this, I don't have a strong opinion, so try
to keep an open mind --- essentially, this is an experiment in pedagogy,
and it will be interesting to see the outcome.

However, I hope that if things don't work out as expected, the question
will be revisited.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] No plans to remove ~
parts:
The dev team is split on this one. I think we understand
the tradeoffs:

* removing it will break backward compatibility and make
Stan programs more verbose (as well as annoying most users
and some developers)

* leaving it in will lead to continued misunderstandings
about what a Stan program does (and annoy all the developers)

What we don't know is how annoyed which groups of people
will be.

In any case, it's not going to even be deprecated any time soon.
2.10 will have a bunch of language changes to support removing ~,
but we're not even all the way there yet (we still need explicit
function calls to log pmfs and log pdfs that drop constants).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] On the coming deprecation of ~
parts:
> On Jun 10, 2016, at 1:39 AM, Tamas Papp <tkp...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> If I understand correctly, the key problem with ~ is that by hiding the
> fact that it increments the log density, it confuses people who don't
> understand the basics of Bayesian inference.

The main issue is that we routinely see Stan code such as

model {
real y;
y ~ normal(0, 1); // rejects because y is not defined

where the author was expecting normal(0, 1) to act like a random number
generator. Instead, they get a not-a-number warning.

We think it might be clearer if they had to write this:

real y;
target += normal_lpdf(y | 0, 1); // also rejects

This latter syntax has been merged into the develop branch of Stan,
so will be in 2.10.

But we're not even deprecating ~ in 2.10.

Another alternative will be to make sure that variables are defined
before they are used. The only way to define a variable in Stan is to have
it show up on the left-hand side of an assignment statement, so it
should be easy to detect.

- Bob
